full_judgment: 10. I have heard the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners and the opposite parties and perused the revisional application along with other materials on record. It appears that according to the plaintiff one Abdul Mannan was the owner of the suit land. The plaintiffs claim their .26 decimals of land from C.S. Dag No.310 C.S. Khatian, exhibit 2, stands in the name of Ram Chandra Shaha and others. There is no document to show that the C.S. recorded tenants made transfer of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs or their predecessors-in-interest in any way. The plaintiffs also claimed that Abdul Mannan filed O.C. Suit No. 25. of 1954 for recovery of khas possession and the suit was decreed in his favour and the plaintiffs purchased the suit land subsequently from Abdul Mannan by virtue of a deed, exhibit-3(ga). The Courts below found that there is no documents on record to show that Abdul Mannan got the suit land from C.S. recorded tenants and there is no basis is no basis of preparation of S.A. record in the name of the plaintiff and Sokiruddin. The Courts below found that the plaintiffs and Sokiruddin. The Courts below found that the plaintiffs and their predecessor acquired no valid title on the suit land there was no legal footing in support of preparation of S.A. or R.S. record and the plaintiffs could not show any dakhila in their favour. It appears that the trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court considered all aspects thoroughly and concurrently found that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case. The decisions of both the Courts below, being based on facts, circumstances and evidence on record and there being concurrent findings over the points in issues and there being found no error of law or fact in passing the impugned judgment, I am of the opinion that the impugned judgments and decrees do not warrant any interference by this Court.
